subject: Latency-weighted allocation request — SprintBridge launch window
messages:
From: Alex Conway <alex.conway@sprintbridge.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 5 Oct 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: urgent dedicated capacity for Oct 20-22 launch window

Hannah —

Thanks again for the call this morning. We are on track for a soft launch of SprintBridge 2.0, and we need a short-term dedicated capacity reservation for Oct 20-22 to guarantee p99 latency under load for our inference-heavy workflows. The attach'd launch plan has traffic forecasts and the GPU sizing we modeled.

Important context: we expect 2 peak hours per day where latency sensitivity is high (interactive demos), and overall batch inference overnight. We can tolerate reduced concurrency outside those demo windows.

Can Redwood commit to an isolated pool for that three-day window? If not fully isolated, we'd accept a latency-weighted allocation policy that prioritizes SprintBridge traffic during the demo windows.

Appreciate a fast confirmation — our execs need the runway.

Regards,
Alex Conway
Head of Infrastructure, SprintBridge
Attachments: sprintbridge-launch-plan-v2.pdf, requested-vCPU-GPU-sheet.csv

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Karhtik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Conway <alex.conway@sprintbridge.com>
Date: Tue, 5 Oct 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Request: urgent dedicated capacity for Oct 20-22 launch window

Team —

Forwarding SprintBridge's ask (below). Key asks: a short-term isolated pool for Oct 20-22, or a policy to prioritize their traffic during two demo windows per day. Their traffic profile shows strong diurnal peaks.

Karthik — can you confirm if we have spare headroom in the us-west pools, or whether we can create a short-lived tranche without impacting existing committed customers? If we can't do full isolation, what's the lowest-risk latency-weighted allocation scheme we can offer that still meets our SLAs for other customers?

Marcus — what's the minimum commercial commitment/credit we should propose to make this workable? SprintBridge is in active negotiations for a Dedicated annual contract, but this is a short-term request that could materially influence the deal.

Monica — can you own the operational runbook/hand-off if we grant this window? We'll need a day-of escalation plan.

I propose we triage options and get back to Alex within 24 hours.

Thanks,
Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Customer Success (Enterprise)
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Conway <alex.conway@sprintbridge.com>
Date: Tue, 5 Oct 2027 13:18:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Request: urgent dedicated capacity for Oct 20-22 launch window

Hannah / team —

Quick technical read:
- Current us-west dedicated pools are ~85% committed for Oct 20-22 with forecasted reserved load (committed customers + scheduled bursts). We have a ~15% headroom, but that is fragmented across racks and not contiguous for full-isolation.
- Creating an isolated tranche on short notice has two operational risks: (1) cold-start provisioning (~6–12 hours per node for validation) and (2) rebalancing live KV caches -> transient latency spikes.

Proposed options (ranked by operational risk):
1) Latency-weighted QoS policy (low risk): implement an ingress policy that tags SprintBridge requests during the two demo windows and gives them weighted priority for GPU slots plus reserved preemptible token buckets outside the windows. Latency SLOs can be preserved for others via bounded preemption quotas. Minimal infra changes; can be enabled in ~24 hours if we accept short-lived policy flags.

2) Soft-isolation (medium risk): carve out a short-lived tranche by shifting flexible burst capacity into a named pool; requires orchestrator approval and a 12–18 hour provisioning window. We'll need to drain some best-effort bursts from low-priority commitments.

3) Full isolation (high risk): stand up dedicated nodes for SprintBridge. Would require a 48+ hour lead time and likely impact some burst commitments and active customers. Recommend only for multi-week windows.

Mitigations: pre-warm KV caches with sample workloads, schedule a pre-launch smoke test Oct 18 morning, and add a fallback policy to route demo traffic to a compatible quantized model variant if latency increases.

I'll run quant/throughput simulations on their supplied CSV and share expected p95/p99 latency curves by EOD.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Conway <alex.conway@sprintbridge.com>
Date: Tue, 5 Oct 2027 15:46:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Request: urgent dedicated capacity for Oct 20-22 launch window

Hannah / Alex —

From a commercial lens: SprintBridge is mid-stage in the dedicated deal (DBL-9743). For a short 3-day reservation, recommend we ask for:
- A bridging credit equal to 25% of the estimated 3-day committed cost, applied if they sign the annual Dedicated contract within 30 days.
- A non-refundable $10k operational fee to cover runbook/eng ops support and smoke testing.
- If we enable latency-weighted QoS rather than full isolation, include an explicit SLA carve-out that commits Redwood to p99 latency during demo windows or customer gets pro-rated credits.

This gives us commercial protection and incentive for SprintBridge to close the longer-term deal. Happy to iterate numbers depending on technical feasibility.

-Marcus
Marcus Lin
Director, Sales — Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Alex Conway <alex.conway@sprintbridge.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 6 Oct 2027 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Request: urgent dedicated capacity for Oct 20-22 launch window

Alex —

Thanks for the details and the attachments. Quick update from our side:
- We can deliver Option 1 (latency-weighted QoS) within ~24 hours. This would prioritize your demo-window traffic while preserving bounded preemption for other customers.
- We can also offer Option 2 (soft-isolation) but it requires us to reassign burst capacity; that has a ~12–18 hour ops window and a small chance of transient cache effects.

Commercially, Marcus suggests a bridging credit (25% of 3-day cost) + $10k operational fee. If SprintBridge signs the annual Dedicated contract within 30 days, the credit applies.

Operational next steps I propose:
1) Approve Option 1 now so we can flip the QoS flag and run a smoke test Oct 18 morning.
2) If you want stronger isolation, tell us by Oct 15 and we'll attempt Option 2 (soft-isolation) and confirm whether we can avoid transient spikes.
3) Sign the attached short SOW for the three-day window covering the ops fee.

Can you confirm today so we can schedule the smoke test?

Best,
Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Customer Success (Enterprise)
Redwood Inference

From: Alex Conway <alex.conway@sprintbridge.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 7 Oct 2027 17:01:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Request: urgent dedicated capacity for Oct 20-22 launch window

Hannah —

Thanks — SprintBridge accepts Option 1 (latency-weighted QoS) and approves the Oct 18 smoke test. We'll sign the short SOW for the 3-day window; please route the SOW and the $10k invoice to our procurement contact: Jen Park <jen.park@sprintbridge.com>.

We also want to lock the Oct 20 10:00–12:00 PT demo window as highest priority. If you can confirm the flag and provide a short runbook checklist, we will circulate internally.

Appreciate the quick coordination — looking forward to the smoke test.

Alex
Alex Conway
Head of Infrastructure, SprintBridge
summary: SprintBridge requested a short-term capacity reservation for an Oct 20-22 launch window. Internal discussion evaluated three options: latency-weighted QoS (low risk), soft-isolation (medium), and full isolation (high). Team recommended Option 1 for 24-hour delivery, with commercial bridging credit + $10k ops fee. SprintBridge accepted Option 1 and scheduled an Oct 18 smoke test; procurement contact provided for SOW/invoice. Action items: Karthik to run simulations and flip QoS flag, Monica to prepare runbook and smoke test plan, Marcus to draft SOW/credit language.
